title: A recurring whole distributes a predicate over members rather than forming one collective
summary: Use the GDT238 array/group relation observation to test whether a recurring whole scopes a predicate distributively over independently typed members, rather than naming one collective group or simply marking an array frame.

design.mechanism: A candidate contributes distributive quantification: the following predicate applies separately to each member in a bounded list.
design.unit: Complete candidate occurrences with independently typed list members, predicate assignments, and collective-versus-distributive interpretation.
design.contrast: candidate-bearing distributed-member contexts versus collective group contexts and candidate-free lists with the same member count and predicate frame.
design.prediction: Candidate contexts should license independently typed member-level predicate attachment or truth conditions, even when every member receives the same predicate outcome. A collective/group model licenses only a group-level predicate; heterogeneous outcomes are useful contrasts but are not required.
design.falsifier: The distributive hypothesis fails if independently bound held cases show that candidate-bearing lists consistently lack member-level predicate scope and are licensed only at group level after matching list size and frame. Uniform member outcomes, repeated fields, or an observed collective-looking result alone do not falsify distributivity.
design.availability: Independent member typing, predicate assignment, and quantifier-scope endpoint availability_unknown; GDT238 explicitly warns that ARRAY_OR_GROUP is a visible relation class, not an established relation word.
design.related: Related to IDEA000032 coordination marker and IDEA000021 amount/unit role, but distinct: this target is member-level quantifier scope, not merely list grouping or a material-independent amount slot. A coordination marker may coexist with either distributive or collective interpretation.
design.countermodel: A renderer can emit repeated member-level fields for a collective group without encoding distributivity; list size, array layout, or register can mimic the predicted member pattern.

source_evidence.quote:
The relation inventory is highly asymmetric:

| relation class | rows |
|---|---:|
| PROXIMITY | 225 |
| ATTACHMENT | 73 |
| ENCLOSURE_OR_CONTACT | 7 |
| ARRAY_OR_GROUP | 5 |

Most stable-prefix occurrences are proximity descriptions.  The gain is only
five rows, so it is not evidence for a rich relation vocabulary.  Exact raw
families provide an important counterexample: on 112 cross-folio-covered rows
they score 65 correct versus 80 for the section baseline (`-.134`), with 6
paired wins and 21 losses.
